searchText: ethers states that `tx.gasPrice` can now be `null` here: https://twitter.com/ethersproject/status/1408836914141138946?s=20 It looks like there now needs to be `if (tx.gasPrice === null)` checks added to code that builds on ethers WIP pull request on web3.js here: https://github.com/ChainSafe/web3.js/pull/4155, it seems like your library is built on ethers based on the `null` value but it is called `web3-core-helpers` <@358385024573243393> Why `null` instead of missing? What do you mean? There are still networks that aren’t EIP-1559. And there always might be, like xdai or BSC. I don’t actually know if they are or not, but I can’t remove the `gasPrice` property from them. ```ts { gasPrice: bigint | null, nonce: bigint, ... } ```vs ```ts { gasPrice: bigint, nonce: bigint, ... } | { nonce: bigint, ... } ``` An EIP-1559 transaction doesn't have a `null` gasPrice, it is that a gasPrice field on an EIP-1559 transaction doesn't make sense at all. IMO, idiomatic JS/TS would be to leave the field off entirely so users can do `if ('gasPrice' in transaction) handleLegacy() else handle1559()` (though really they should be switching on the transaction type). Oh, I thought you mean removed from the typing. It is hard to do that with the way the code is currently designed. There is a formatted with a descriptor that does all the parsing. gasPrice went from `bigNumberish` to `allowNull(bigNumberish)`. But I generally don’t plan around people relying on auto-vivification as a method for value discovery. Because sometime auto-vivification happens. So, I expect people to check for nullish, via `if (tx.gasPrice == null)` which catches both, “missing” or null. Also, if you use a union set it would be massive. 2 ** 9 ish sets right now, at least. In v6 many things become `gasPrice?: BigNumberish | null` for input and `gasPrice: null | BigNumber` for output. <@255928837727059979> after a quick look at your code, I think there are bugs in the signTransaction. If accessList is defined, it will use EIP-2930 and then else if maxFeePerGas use EIP-1559. But EIP-1559 can also have an access list, in which case you have already knee-capped EIP-1559. 😒 There is a lot of conditions requires to auto detect the type. And you actually probably want to detect the networks capabilities first. For example, if talking to an EIP-1559 network, your default should be 1559 if there isn’t enough info to determine type. It was a lot of back-and-forth and I implemented that populateTransaction 12 or so different ways before settling on that. Nothing was perfect. It was about least terrible. 🙂 Also, in v6 getGasPrice will go away and you will need to use `(await provider.getFeeData()).gasPrice` for the legacy gasPrice. All fee-related things will be bundled into the `provider.getFeeData()` method. Just a heads up. 🙂 If you mean that web3.js PR, that isn't mine but I'm sure they would like to hear your feedback 🙂 Oh, thanks. 😉

excerpts.author: tyneslol
excerpts.content:
ethers states that `tx.gasPrice` can now be `null` here:
https://twitter.com/ethersproject/status/1408836914141138946?s=20
It looks like there now needs to be `if (tx.gasPrice === null)` checks added to code that builds on ethers
WIP pull request on web3.js here: https://github.com/ChainSafe/web3.js/pull/4155, it seems like your library is built on ethers based on the `null` value but it is called `web3-core-helpers`

excerpts.content: There are still networks that aren’t EIP-1559.

excerpts.author: ricmoo
excerpts.content: And there always might be, like xdai or BSC. I don’t actually know if they are or not, but I can’t remove the `gasPrice` property from them.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
sky.cactus
excerpts.content: An EIP-1559 transaction doesn't have a `null` gasPrice, it is that a gasPrice field on an EIP-1559 transaction doesn't make sense at all.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: IMO, idiomatic JS/TS would be to leave the field off entirely so users can do `if ('gasPrice' in transaction) handleLegacy() else handle1559()` (though really they should be switching on the transaction type).

excerpts.author: ricmoo
excerpts.content: Oh, I thought you mean removed from the typing. It is hard to do that with the way the code is currently designed. There is a formatted with a descriptor that does all the parsing. gasPrice went from `bigNumberish` to `allowNull(bigNumberish)`.

excerpts.author: ricmoo
excerpts.content: But I generally don’t plan around people relying on auto-vivification as a method for value discovery. Because sometime auto-vivification happens. So, I expect people to check for nullish, via `if (tx.gasPrice == null)` which catches both, “missing” or null.

excerpts.author: ricmoo
excerpts.content: Also, if you use a union set it would be massive. 2 ** 9 ish sets right now, at least.

excerpts.author: ricmoo
excerpts.content: In v6 many things become `gasPrice?: BigNumberish | null` for input and `gasPrice: null | BigNumber` for output.

If accessList is defined, it will use EIP-2930 and then else if maxFeePerGas use EIP-1559. But EIP-1559 can also have an access list, in which case you have already knee-capped EIP-1559. 😒

excerpts.content: There is a lot of conditions requires to auto detect the type. And you actually probably want to detect the networks capabilities first. For example, if talking to an EIP-1559 network, your default should be 1559 if there isn’t enough info to determine type.
